A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nodal roots with more aerenchymatous cortical cells and larger lacunae are associated with increased mycorrhizae but decreased pathogenic fungal colonization, whereas roots with smaller cortical cells and smaller lacunae are more prone to root rot and F. verticillioides colonization.

the tradeoffs of root cortical anatomy on pathogenic and mutualistic fungi are not straightforward, and that root anatomy may be an adaptive trait that can be manipulated to alter root colonization patterns.
